hero.title:
Secrets safe,

team happy.
hero.subtitle: Secret management with Zero-Knowledge encryption. Your .env files are encrypted before they ever leave your machine.

zeroKnowledge.title: Zero-Knowledge
zeroKnowledge.description: AES-GCM 256-bit encryption client-side. The server NEVER sees your secrets in plain text.

cli.title: Remote CLI
cli.description: The terminal works directly against the remote vault: login, project, set, get, list, import and export without mirroring secrets into a local SQLite file.

teamSync.title: Team Sync
teamSync.description: CLI, web dashboard, team and CI/CD all work from the same encrypted source of truth, per project and environment.

control.title: Full control
control.description: Audit logs, roles, invites, CI tokens, API keys, OAuth, 2FA and Vercel/Render integrations without exposing plaintext.

workflow.label: How It Works
workflow.title: One remote vault. <accent>Zero plaintext on the server.</accent>
workflow.description: CriptEnv acts as a remote terminal for your project vault: you authenticate, unlock with the Vault password and sync only encrypted blobs between CLI, web, team and CI.

panel.title: From terminal to deploy, the API only coordinates ciphertext.

proofs: API sees ciphertext, IV and metadata

authenticate.title: Authenticate the terminal
authenticate.description: The session stays protected locally as metadata. Secrets still require the Vault password of the project.

createVault.title: Create the project vault
createVault.description: The Vault password is born on the client, derives the environment keys and is never sent to the API.

writeSecrets.title: Write secrets to the remote vault
writeSecrets.description: The CLI decrypts in memory, changes the set, re-encrypts and pushes only versioned ciphertext.

consume.title: Use it on the web, with the team or in CI
consume.description: List keys, export files when needed and hand secrets to your pipeline without creating a parallel local vault.

pricing.label: Pricing
pricing.title: Start free. Upgrade when you need to.

cta.label: Get Started
cta.title: Ship your first secure vault to production.
cta.description: Create an account, connect the CLI and invite your team once the remote vault is sealed. No confusing trial, no plaintext on the server.

problemToVault.title: From a loose .env to a sealed vault
problemToVault.description: CriptEnv takes variables scattered across machines, applies authenticated local encryption and syncs only opaque blobs. The vault becomes the auditable source of truth; plaintext never crosses the network.

platformPreview.title: You only see <accent>results.</accent>
platformPreview.desktopAlt: CriptEnv dashboard showing projects, secrets, team and audit

security.label: Security
security.title: One vault explained in four layers
security.intro: On mobile the story stacks so reading, touch and scroll control are preserved. The story is the same: encrypt locally, sync ciphertext and keep everything auditable.

aesGcm.title: AES-GCM
aesGcm.description: Every secret becomes ciphertext using AES-GCM with a 256-bit key. GCM mode combines confidentiality and authentication: if anyone changes bytes, nonce or auth tag, decryption fails instead of returning corrupted data.
details: Unique nonce per operation and a 128-bit auth tag to detect tampering.
The server stores encrypted blobs, never .env values in cleartext.
aesGcm.imageAlt: Illustration of the AES standard with an encrypted folder

zeroKnowledge.title: Zero-knowledge
zeroKnowledge.kicker: The backend runs without knowing the secret
zeroKnowledge.description: CriptEnv Cloud receives only ciphertext, operational metadata and the trails needed for synchronization. Decryption keys stay off the server, so the database, the API and the logs never hold enough material to reveal your secrets.
details: Plaintext never crosses the network boundary.
Content keys are never sent to the API.
The server coordinates access and versions without seeing the real value.

clientSide.title: Client-side only
clientSide.kicker: The key is born and works on the device
clientSide.description: The project password derives keys locally with PBKDF2/HKDF, and encryption happens before any push. The crypto store is not persisted to localStorage, which reduces exposure from XSS or a reused session.
details: PBKDF2 strengthens the password before deriving the master key.
HKDF separates keys by environment and context.
Values are only decrypted on the authorized client.
clientSide.imageAlt: A set of master keys on a transparent background

openSource.title: 100% open source and auditable
openSource.kicker: Trust by inspection, not by promise
openSource.description: The code is open under the MIT license so teams can review the encryption flow, validate security decisions and follow changes. The product audit trail records actions without turning secrets into sensitive evidence.
details: Open implementation to read, fork and review.
Crypto flow verifiable locally by whoever runs the project.
Audit logs track actions and context without recording plaintext.
openSource.imageAlt: Golden checklist representing review and audit
